units.en: Biographies of Wei Cao, Mo Han, and Liu Kuren
units.literal: Wei Cao; Mo Han; Liu Kuren

units.en: Wei Cao, whose style was Deyuan, came from Dai.
units.literal: Wei Cao, styled Deyuan, was a man of Dai.

units.en: As a young man he lived by the code of the knight-errant and showed both talent and strategic mind.
units.literal: In youth he mastered chivalry and possessed talent and stratagem.

units.zh: 晉征北將軍衞瓘以操為牙門將，數使於國，頗自結附。
units.en: Jin's General Who Pacifies the North, Wei Guan, appointed Cao gate officer and often sent him on missions to the Dai state, where Cao gradually built ties of his own.
units.literal: Jin General Who Pacifies the North Wei Guan made Cao a gate officer; he was repeatedly sent to the state and rather attached himself on his own.

units.zh: 始祖崩後，與從子雄及其宗室鄉親姬澹等十數人，同來歸國，說桓穆二帝招納晉人，於是晉人附者稍眾。
units.en: When the founding ancestor passed away, Cao came home with his nephew Xiong and a dozen-odd kinsmen and neighbors, among them Ji Dan, and urged the Huan and Mu emperors to welcome Jin subjects. From then on Jin adherents grew steadily in number.
units.literal: After the founding ancestor died, together with his nephew Xiong and more than ten clansmen and fellow-townsmen such as Ji Dan, he came in a body to return to the state, urging the Huan and Mu emperors to recruit Jin people; thereafter those of Jin who attached themselves grew somewhat numerous.

units.zh: 桓帝嘉之，以為輔相，任以國事。
units.en: Emperor Huan approved and named him chief minister, charging him with the affairs of the realm.
units.literal: Emperor Huan commended this and made him chief minister, entrusting him with state affairs.

units.zh: 及劉淵、石勒之亂，勸桓帝匡助晉氏。
units.en: When Liu Yuan and Shi Le threw the north into rebellion, he pressed Emperor Huan to stand with the house of Jin.
units.literal: When the disorders of Liu Yuan and Shi Le arose, he urged Emperor Huan to support and aid the Jin house.

units.zh: 東瀛公司馬騰聞而善之，表加將號。
units.en: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing this, praised the policy and memorialized the throne to grant Cao further military rank.
units.literal: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command, hearing of it, approved and memorialized to add military titles.

units.zh: 稍遷至右將軍，封定襄侯。
units.en: He rose in stages to Right General and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.
units.literal: He was gradually promoted to Right General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang.

units.zh: 桓帝崩後，操立碑於大邗城南，[1]以頌功德，云：「魏，軒轅之苗裔。」
units.en: After Emperor Huan's death, Cao set up a monument south of Da Hang and [1], to hymn his achievements, began: "The Wei are offspring of the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan."
units.literal: After Emperor Huan died, Cao erected a stele south of Da Hang city, [1] to praise his merit and virtue, saying: "Wei, a scion of Xuanyuan."

units.zh: 言：桓穆二帝「馳名域外，九譯宗焉。
units.en: Of the Huan and Mu emperors it reads: "Their renown rides beyond the frontier; peoples of nine interpreters bow to them.
units.literal: It says of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their fame gallops beyond the borders; nine tongues pay them homage.

units.en: In ruling the realm and commanding the people, their majesty and law ran everywhere.
units.literal: Governing the state and ruling the masses, awe and prohibition go forth in full force.

units.en: Their name shone among the Chinese lineages and matched the light of highest spirit.
units.literal: Their sound stands out among the Hua tribes; they share radiance with pure numen.

units.zh: 智深謀遠，窮幽極明，治則清斷，沉浮得情。
units.en: Deep in wisdom, far in counsel, they sounded the dark and touched the farthest light; in rule they were lucid and decisive, and in fortune's turns they read the truth of each case.
units.literal: Wisdom deep, plans far-reaching, probing the hidden and reaching the utmost bright; in governing, clear judgment; in rise and fall, grasping the heart of things.

units.en: Their grace was the spring sun; their sternness, autumn frost.
units.literal: Benevolence like the spring sun; awesomeness like autumn's frost.

units.en: The mighty did not crush the meek; they sheltered orphans and the forsaken.
units.literal: The strong did not bully the weak; they hid away care for the orphaned and alone.

units.en: The Way they taught was humane action; they changed hearts without the lash.
units.literal: The Way taught benevolent conduct; they transformed without punishments.

units.en: No traitor or thief walked the land; along the roads people sang their praise.
units.literal: Within the state no treachery or theft; on the roads, songs of praise.

units.en: From west to east their influence shifted like formless change.
units.literal: From west to east, change without form.

units.en: Where their arms pointed, no foe dared meet them in the field.
units.literal: Wherever martial might was aimed, below them no armies crossed.

units.en: To the south they upheld the imperial house; to the north they brought the Dingling to heel.
units.literal: South they unified the royal house; north they made the Dingling submit.

units.en: They called and taught the six Di peoples, and all returned in good faith.
units.literal: They summoned and instructed the six Di; all came in returning sincerity.

units.en: Outdoing the past and unmatched thereafter, they brought this triumph into being.
units.literal: Surpassing what went before and cutting off what came after, they brought this achievement to pass.

units.en: They served the Jin sovereign and held the marches against invasion.
units.literal: They upheld the Jin emperor and defended the frontier borders.

units.en: The imperial house knew many calamities; the net of heaven hung loose.
units.literal: The royal house had many hardships; heaven's net slackened its cords.

units.en: With heroic hearts they aided from afar and would not abandon Jin in its ruin.
units.literal: With heroic hearts they aided from afar and did not leave its afflictions.

units.en: Each year they struck down rebellion; traitors and bandits prowled like wolves.
units.literal: Year by year they cut down rebellious fate; traitors and thieves were wolves and jackals.

units.en: In the first year of Yong'an, the cycle stood at jiazi.
units.literal: Yong'an year one, the year star at jiazi.

units.en: The rebel clique still defied the throne; east and west, foes crouched like wolves.
units.literal: The traitor faction still rebelled; east and west wolves stood at bay.

units.en: They dared harry the Son of Heaven; war flared up time after time.
units.literal: They dared press the Son of Heaven; arms and armor rose again and again.

units.en: Trusting their numbers, they rampaged and abused officers and men.
units.literal: Relying on their numbers they indulged in violence and cruelly used the commanders and soldiers.

units.en: Ye and Luoyang split in discord; they forsook their own to court strangers.
units.literal: Ye and Luoyang met with rifts; they cast off kin to seek the distant.

units.en: Then they called in savage allies: the Tuge and the Xiongnu.
units.literal: Then they recruited violent sorts—the Tuge and the Xiongnu.

units.en: Liu Yuan the renegade joined their faction and shouted with one voice.
units.literal: Liu Yuan the traitorous villain banded with them in common cry.

units.en: They dared strike into Bing and slaughter the innocent.
units.literal: They dared strike Bing province and slaughter the guiltless.

units.en: Devastation spread like trampled fields; towns were heaped into rubble.
units.literal: Ruin and breakage lay like scattered reeds; cities and towns became mounds and ruins.

units.en: For a thousand li blades crossed; a long serpent of war choked the highways.
units.literal: Blades crossed for a thousand li; a long serpent blocked the road.

units.en: Jin's mandate answered heaven; its counsel opened sound designs.
units.literal: Jin's Way answered heaven; its words unfolded good plans.

units.zh: 使持節、平北將軍、并州刺史、護匈奴中郎將、東瀛公司馬騰，才神絕世，規略超遠。
units.en: Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command—Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing, Protector of the Xiongnu—was a genius without peer, his designs reaching beyond the horizon.
units.literal: Bearer of the staff of office, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing province, Protector of the Xiongnu, Sima Teng of the Eastern Garrison command—talent and spirit unmatched in the age, strategy and layout surpassing the far horizon.

units.en: Disaster piled upon disaster; he feared the altars of Jin would fall.
units.literal: The times met with many hardships; he feared harm to the imperial sacrifices.

units.en: He meant to march out with his host, but the northern Xianyun raged fierce.
units.literal: He wished to lead troops forth; the Xianyun burned fierce.

units.en: He forged expedients and strange counsel to break the siege of calamity.
units.literal: He devised expedient measures and plans to aid the hardship with wondrous thought.

units.en: He sought aid from beyond the court, but no minister at court would answer.
units.literal: He wished to summon outside rescue; the court ministers none responded.

units.en: Alone he weighed the heights and fixed the plan of alliance.
units.literal: With high calculation he decided alone and settled the plan of alliance.

units.en: Then he charged the outer state to bring its armies in as a reserve within.
units.literal: Thereupon he ordered the foreign state to lead troops within as reserve.

units.en: He chose the able and picked knights and named them bearers of this charge.
units.literal: He selected worthy men and chose knights and appointed them envoys of this good mission.

units.zh: 遣參軍壺倫、牙門中行嘉、義陽亭侯衞謨、協義亭侯衞鞬等，馳奉檄書，至晉陽城。」
units.en: He dispatched Staff Officer Hu Lun, gate officer Zhonghang Jia, Marquis of Yiyang Ting Wei Mo, Marquis of Xieyi Ting Wei Jian, and others to race the imperial summons to Jinyang."
units.literal: He sent Staff Officer Hu Lun, gate officer Zhonghang Jia, Marquis of Yiyang Ting Wei Mo, Marquis of Xieyi Ting Wei Jian, and others, galloping with the proclamation document to Jinyang city."

units.zh: 又稱：桓穆二帝「心在宸極。
units.en: Again of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their hearts clung to the imperial pole.
units.literal: Again it says of the Huan and Mu emperors: "Their hearts were at the polar throne.

units.en: The two Wei ministers stood as paired wings to lift the throne.
units.literal: The two Weis as chief ministers faced and raised, wing to wing.

units.en: Cao laid out plans in letters; Xiong flamed in deeds of war.
units.literal: Cao unfolded literary stratagems; Xiong roused martial valor.

units.en: Ordered to council, they debated with fire in their speech.
units.literal: Receiving the command they met in council; in consultation and debate they blazed forth.

units.en: Of old Duke Huan of Qi had aided the throne, and his merit shone in the annals of Zhou.
units.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi aided and his merit stood out in the Zhou house.

units.en: His fame filled the records; rewards and gifts were heaped upon him.
units.literal: Illustrious names were loaded on the registers; ranks of reward and full gifts were complete.

units.en: The great army wheeled into motion; glory gathered as though spirits had convened.
units.literal: The great host turned and moved; splendor gathered like spirits.

units.en: They mustered a million men, promising victory within a day.
units.literal: They raised an army of a million; the term was not to pass a single day.

units.en: Brothers bound in one oath, they settled victory in the war council of the temple.
units.literal: Brothers in one pact, they decided victory in the temple's calculation.

units.en: With drums and battle-cry they marched south and smoothed away danger and hardship."
units.literal: Beating drums and clamor they marched south and leveled the perilous and hard."

units.zh: 又云：二帝到鎮，「言若合符。
units.en: It adds: when the two emperors took the field, "their words matched like split tally-sticks.
units.literal: Again it says: when the two emperors reached their command post, "words like matching tallies.

units.en: They received each other in close trust; faith and duty never wavered.
units.literal: They drew in with intimate good faith; trust and righteousness never shifted.

units.en: They swore alliance east of the Fen and cut the oath in vermilion on stone.
units.literal: They allied east of the Fen and inscribed the covenant in cinnabar script.

units.en: To serve forever; to guard the bond at the end as at the beginning.
units.literal: Forever to uphold and serve; careful at the end as at the first.

units.en: The sworn pact set the generals marching; picked warriors rode in the van.
units.literal: The covenant charged the generals; elite sharpness led the van.

units.en: Southward they relieved Nie; eastward they broke the siege of Shouyang.
units.literal: South they rescued Nie county; east they relieved Shouyang.

units.en: Cities that had sunk into darkness burned bright again.
units.literal: Straitened towns, darkened, then shone again with light.

units.zh: 太原、西河，樂平、上黨，遽遭寇暴，白骨交橫。
units.en: Taiyuan, Xihe, Leping, and Shangdang were suddenly ravaged; the dead lay in crossed heaps of bone.
units.literal: Taiyuan, Xihe, Leping, and Shangdang suddenly met with bandit violence; white bones lay crossed.

units.en: Jie raiders ran riot; six commanderies were laid waste.
units.literal: The Jie bandits ran wild; the six commanderies withered in harm.

units.en: Evil men answered one another in crowds; their plot aimed at the throne room itself.
units.literal: The wicked in throngs answered one another; their plot reached the splendid hall.

units.en: At a light signal of banners the Jie hosts shattered and fell.
units.literal: Banners and flags lightly pointed; the Jie faction broke and perished.

units.en: Ten thousand horsemen were sent ahead to the banks of the Qi and Zhang.
units.literal: They sent ten thousand horsemen to advance before them to the Qi and Zhang rivers.

units.en: Ye shook apart and collapsed; the traitors fled in rout.
units.literal: Ye then shook apart and collapsed; the vicious rebels ran and fled.

units.en: The army held the southern commanderies; their bright spears pointed at the Taihang.
units.literal: The army held the south of the province; their gleaming blades faced the Taihang.

units.en: They shielded the realm within and without and stilled the four quarters.
units.literal: Wing and guard within and without; they quieted the four quarters.

units.en: Their will was to spend their last strength upholding the Son of Heaven.
units.literal: Their will was to exhaust their strength and uphold and carry the Son of Heaven.

units.en: Loyalty and forbearance lit the age; stirred from without, they drove the foe back as well.
units.literal: Loyalty and forbearance shone forth; stirred from without, they also repelled.

units.en: Then they flaunted their arms, rallied the columns, and marched home.
units.literal: Thereupon they displayed martial might and, shaking the host, turned and returned.

units.en: The road was long and strange; their going and coming spanned a year.
units.literal: The long road was not of the Yi; going out and entering took a full year.

units.en: Not a hair of the people was harmed; folk praised them on every tongue.
units.literal: Not a hair was violated; the common people spread their praise.

units.en: They searched the loaded annals from antiquity to their own day.
units.literal: They perused the loaded records from antiquity down to the present.

units.en: Never had they read of a border people racing inward to save an imperial crisis.
units.literal: They had not heard of an outer domain rushing to rescue an inner affliction.

units.en: They left their homes and grieved for the realm, trading peril for peace.
units.literal: They abandoned family and grieved for the state, exchanging danger for peace.

units.en: Only the lord's far sight—in hardship he still held authority.
units.literal: Only the duke's far-reaching layout—in facing hardship could wield power.

units.en: He answered heaven and followed the people; grace and virtue had long been proclaimed.
units.literal: Answering heaven and following the people, grace and virtue long proclaimed.

units.en: He made peace with the Rong and stilled the north; the realm in peril lived again."
units.literal: He harmonized the Rong and quieted the north; the endangered state was restored."

units.zh: 又云：「非桓天挺，忠孝自然。
units.en: It also says: "Huan was endowed by Heaven, loyal and filial by nature.
units.literal: It also says: "Huan was endowed by Heaven, loyal and filial by nature.

units.en: Who else could transcend the ordinary without becoming an aberration?
units.literal: Who could transcend the ordinary and not become a strange aberration?

units.en: He stirred the multitude, moved by the lord's words.
units.literal: He turned and moved the multitude, who were stirred by the lord's words.

units.en: His merit aided a whole province, and his achievements shone far and wide.
units.literal: His merit aided a whole province, and his achievements shone and spread.

units.en: In days of peace, he offered tribute and strengthened the frontier.
units.literal: In days of peace, he offered tribute and filled the frontier.

units.en: Trusting in them, he looked toward the imperial canopies and set foot in the Three Rivers.
units.literal: Leaning on them, he looked toward the imperial canopies and set foot in the Three Rivers.

units.en: He had virtue but no allotted fortune, and his great span did not extend.
units.literal: He had virtue but no allotted fortune; his great span did not extend.

units.zh: 年三十有九，以永興二年六月二十四日，寢疾薨殂。
units.en: At thirty-nine, on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of Yongxing year 2, he fell ill and died.
units.literal: At age thirty-nine, on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of Yongxing year 2, he fell ill and died.

units.en: He left behind the splendid hall and the famed capital of Yunzhong.
units.literal: He turned his back on the splendid hall, the famed capital in Yunzhong.

units.en: The state lost a kindly lord; grief stirred sobs and sighs.
units.literal: The state lost a kindly lord; grief moved sobs and sighs.

units.en: Sorrow and pain, anguish and wrong: they wailed and cried.
units.literal: Sorrow and pain, vexation and anguish: they wailed and cried.

units.en: The whole state collapsed in despair, clutching for support with nowhere to appeal.
units.literal: The whole state collapsed in despair, clutching for support with nowhere to appeal.

units.en: Far and near followed the same road, hurrying to the coffin hut.
units.literal: Far and near followed the same road, hurrying to the coffin hut.

units.en: People would have given a hundred lives for his one, filling and blocking the gates and roads.
units.literal: People would have given a hundred lives for his one, filling and blocking gate and road.

units.en: The high mountain had fallen; the luxuriant forest had withered.
units.literal: The high mountain had fallen; the luxuriant forest had withered.

units.en: They looked up and appealed to Creation, pain prolonging their grief."
units.literal: They looked up and appealed to Creation, pain prolonging their grief."

units.zh: 又云：桓帝「忠於晉室，駿奔長衢。
units.en: Again it says: Emperor Huan "was loyal to the Jin house and hastened along the long road.
units.literal: Again it says: Emperor Huan "was loyal to the Jin house and hastened along the long road.

units.en: In bleak midwinter, he went out in all directions to carry out punishment.
units.literal: In bleak midwinter, he went out in all directions to carry out punishment.

units.en: He braved frost and snow until illness entered his veins and skin.
units.literal: He braved frost and snow, and illness entered his veins and skin.

units.en: Thus he came to die, not prolonging his twilight years.
units.literal: Thus he came to die and fall, not prolonging his twilight years.

units.en: He served diligently unto death, matching the model of meritorious service.
units.literal: He was diligent in service unto death, matching the model of meritorious service.

units.en: His name was handed down on metal and stone, and his excellence was recorded in the Book of Jin.
units.literal: His name was handed down on metal and stone, and his excellence was recorded in the Book of Jin.

units.zh: 平北哀悼，祭以豐厨，考行論勳，諡曰義烈。
units.en: The General Who Pacifies the North mourned him, sacrificed with abundant offerings, examined his conduct and discussed his merit, and gave him the posthumous name Yilie.
units.literal: The General Who Pacifies the North mourned him, sacrificed with abundant kitchens, examined his conduct and discussed his merit, and gave him the posthumous name Yilie.

units.en: His merit benefited the people; it is what the sacrificial canons commend."
units.literal: His merit was bestowed on the people; it is what the sacrificial canons commend."

units.zh: 又云：桓帝經濟，「存亡繼絕。
units.en: Again of Emperor Huan's rule: "He preserved the dying line and continued what had been severed.
units.literal: Again it says of Emperor Huan's governance: "He preserved what was perishing and continued what was cut off.

units.en: The far marches leaned on him; the throne endured unbroken.
units.literal: The wild domains relied on him; the throne endured without ceasing.

units.en: Golden tortoise insignia, reed-pipes and drums, light carriages and marks of special honor.
units.literal: Golden tortoise, reed-pipes and drums, light carriages and special regalia.

units.en: Looking back through two dynasties, none shared his rank.
units.literal: Reaching back to the two dynasties, none stood in the same rank.

units.en: Bing province sighed in praise; the northern lands felt his glory.
units.literal: The Bing region sighed in praise; the northern states felt his glory.

units.en: Each gave his whole heart, eager to lift his noble name.
units.literal: Each exhausted his heart, thinking to raise his fine name.

units.en: They carved stone to record his deeds; painted images kept his likeness.
units.literal: They carved stone to record merit; images preserved his form.

units.en: Sacrifice never ceased; victims were set before him in feast.
units.literal: Without ceasing they offered sacrifice; they feasted him with victims.

units.en: His fame was handed down forever; in death no shade of him was lost.
units.literal: Forever handed down to later ages; when gone, no remnant spirit was left.

units.en: He endures undying; his glory stretches through ages beyond counting."
units.literal: Long preserved without decay; extended for a hundred million ages."

units.zh: 其頌又稱：桓帝「金堅玉剛。
units.en: Its eulogy further states: Emperor Huan "was firm as metal and hard as jade.
units.literal: Its eulogy further states: Emperor Huan "was firm as metal and hard as jade.

units.en: He answered the moment and followed its convergence, ruling in the north.
units.literal: He answered the time and followed its convergence, ruling in the north.

units.en: His conduct aided the state, and his martial power pacified the four wastes.
units.literal: His conduct could aid the state, and his martial power pacified the four wastes.

units.en: None who thought of him failed to submit; the region was greatly at peace.
units.literal: None who thought of him failed to submit; the region was greatly at peace.

units.en: The roads of the age tangled in disorder, and his fortunes met upheaval.
units.literal: The roads of the age tangled in disorder, and his fortunes met dispersal and upheaval.

units.en: The Jie barbarians seized on disorder and dared to harm the lands of Bing.
units.literal: The Jie barbarians seized on disorder and dared to harm Bing's lands.

units.en: He grieved for the common people, dying and driven from their homes.
units.literal: He grieved for the lower people, who were dying and losing their homes.

units.en: He led a million people, leveling dangers and obstacles.
units.literal: He led a million people, leveling dangers and obstacles.

units.en: He preserved the dying and continued the severed, and one province received his blessing.
units.literal: He preserved the dying and continued the severed, and one province received blessing.

units.en: His achievements blazed, dragon-patterned and tiger-martial.
units.literal: His meritorious achievements blazed, dragon-patterned and tiger-martial.

units.en: Zhu Yi's small goodness left love in Tongxiang.
units.literal: Zhu Yi's small goodness left love in Tongxiang.

units.en: His merit drove off a great calamity, and the six commanderies were spared.
units.literal: His merit drove off a great calamity, and the six commanderies were spared.

units.en: After the lacuna, all who came were preserved through his merit.
units.literal: After the lacuna, all who came were preserved through his merit.

units.en: They carved stone and engraved an inscription, handing it down as a display to later descendants."
units.literal: They carved stone and engraved an inscription, handing it down as a display to later descendants."

units.en: This was in the autumn of Jin Guangxi year 1.
units.literal: This was in the autumn of Jin Guangxi year 1.

units.zh: 皇興初，雍州別駕雁門段榮於大邗掘得此碑，文雖非麗，事宜載焉，故錄於傳。
units.en: Early in the Huangxing era, Duan Rong of Yanmen, assistant administrator of Yong province, unearthed this stele at Da Hang. The writing is not elegant, but the events deserve record, and so they are set down here in the biography.
units.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Duan Rong of Yanmen, Assistant in Yong province, dug up this stele at Da Hang; though the text is not beautiful, the matter ought to be recorded, and therefore it is copied into the biography.

units.en: Both Emperor Huan and Emperor Mu treated Cao with high ceremonial honor.
units.literal: The Huan and Mu emperors both honored Cao with ritual weight.

units.en: He died in the third year of Emperor Mu.
units.literal: In Emperor Mu's third year he died.

units.zh: 始操所與宗室鄉親入國者：衞懃，安樂亭侯；
units.en: Those who had first entered the state with Cao among his kinsmen and neighbors included Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Ting;
units.literal: At first, among the clansmen and fellow-townsmen who entered the state with Cao: Wei Qin, Marquis of Anle Ting;

units.en: Wei Chong and Wei Qing were both enfeoffed as Marquises of Du Ting;
units.literal: Wei Chong and Wei Qing, both Marquises of Du Ting;

units.zh: 衞泥、段繁，並信義將軍、都亭侯；
units.en: Wei Ni and Duan Fan held the rank of General of Trust and Righteousness and were Marquises of Du Ting;
units.literal: Wei Ni and Duan Fan, both Generals of Trust and Righteousness and Marquises of Du Ting;

units.en: Wang Fa was made General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Du Ting;
units.literal: Wang Fa, General Who Establishes Martial Might and Marquis of Du Ting;

units.zh: 范班，折衝將軍、廣武亭侯；
units.en: Fan Ban held the rank of General Who Breaks the Enemy and Marquis of Guangwu;
units.literal: Fan Ban, General Who Breaks the Enemy and Marquis of Guangwu;

units.zh: 賈慶，建武將軍、上洛亭侯；
units.en: Jia Qing was General Who Establishes Martial and Marquis of Shangluo;
units.literal: Jia Qing, General Who Establishes Martial and Marquis of Shangluo;

units.en: Jia Xun held commandery marquis rank;
units.literal: Jia Xun, Commandery Marquis;

units.en: Li Yi was enfeoffed Marquis of Guanzhong;
units.literal: Li Yi, Marquis of Guanzhong;

units.en: Guo Ru held the title Marquis Within the Passes.
units.literal: Guo Ru, Marquis Within the Passes.

units.en: Each had received rank and title from Emperor Huan's commendations.
units.literal: All were enfeoffed and appointed by tables from Emperor Huan.

units.zh: 六脩之難，存者多隨劉琨任子遵南奔。
units.en: After the Six Xiu disaster, most survivors fled south with Zun, Liu Kun's designated heir.
units.literal: In the trouble of Six Xiu, most of those who survived followed Liu Kun's heir-son Ziyun in flight south.

units.zh: 衞雄、姬澹、莫含等名，皆見碑。
units.en: Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, Mo Han, and others are all named on the monument.
units.literal: The names of Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, Mo Han, and others all appear on the stele.

units.zh: 雄字世遠，澹字世雅，並勇健多計畫，晉世州從事。
units.en: Xiong's style was Shiyuan, and Dan's was Shiya; both were bold, resourceful men who had served as provincial aides under the Jin.
units.literal: Xiong's style was Shiyuan, Dan's style Shiya; both were brave and strong and full of stratagems, Jin-era provincial aides.

units.zh: 既與衞操俱入國，桓帝壯其膂力，並以為將，常隨征伐，大著威名。
units.en: When they entered the realm with Wei Cao, Emperor Huan was impressed by their strength and made them generals; they fought at his side on campaign after campaign and won a towering reputation.
units.literal: After they entered the state together with Wei Cao, Emperor Huan admired their physical strength and made them both generals; they constantly followed on campaign and won great renown.

units.zh: 桓帝之赴難也，表晉列其勳效，皆拜將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Huan marched to the rescue, he reported their deeds to the Jin court and secured general's commissions for them all.
units.literal: When Emperor Huan went to relieve the crisis, he memorialized the Jin court listing their achievements, and all were appointed generals.

units.zh: 雄連有戰功，稍遷至左將軍、雲中侯。
units.en: Xiong piled victory on victory until he rose to Left General and Marquis of Yunzhong.
units.literal: Xiong repeatedly won in battle and was gradually promoted to Left General and Marquis of Yunzhong.

units.zh: 澹亦以勇績著名，桓帝末，至信義將軍、樓煩侯。
units.en: Dan likewise became famous for martial feats; by the close of Emperor Huan's reign he held General of Faith and Righteousness and Marquis of Loufan.
units.literal: Dan too was famed for courage in action; at the end of Emperor Huan's reign he reached General of Faith and Righteousness and Marquis of Loufan.

units.en: Early in Emperor Mu's reign both were again given weighty trust.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mu's reign both were entrusted with office.

units.zh: 衞操卒後，俱為左右輔相。
units.en: After Wei Cao's death they served together as the left and right hands of government.
units.literal: After Wei Cao died, both became left and right assisting ministers.

units.zh: 六脩之逆，國內大亂，新舊猜嫌，迭相誅戮。
units.en: The Six Xiu revolt threw the realm into chaos; old settlers and new allies eyed one another with suspicion and killed in waves.
units.literal: In the rebellion of Six Xiu the state fell into great disorder; old and new factions nursed suspicion and slaughtered one another in turn.

units.zh: 雄、澹並為羣情所附，謀欲南歸，言於眾曰：「聞諸舊人忌新人悍戰，欲盡殺之，吾等不早為計，恐無種矣。」
units.en: The crowd rallied to Xiong and Dan; they planned a southern flight and told the assembly, "We hear the old faction hates how fiercely the newcomers fight and intends to wipe them out. Unless we act now, our line will end."
units.literal: Xiong and Dan were both attached to by the multitude; they plotted to flee south and said to the assembly: "We hear the old hands resent the newcomers' fierceness in battle and mean to kill them all; if we do not plan early, I fear our line will perish."

units.zh: 晉人及烏丸驚懼，皆曰：「死亡隨二將軍。」
units.en: Jin subjects and Wuhuan alike were terrified and cried, "We live or die with these two generals."
units.literal: Jin men and Wuhuan were alarmed and afraid, and all said: "Death follows the two generals."

units.zh: 於是雄、澹與劉琨任子遵率烏丸、晉人數萬眾而叛。
units.en: Then Xiong and Dan, with Zun, Liu Kun's heir, led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin followers into open revolt.
units.literal: Thereupon Xiong and Dan with Liu Kun's heir-son Ziyun led tens of thousands of Wuhuan and Jin men in revolt.

units.zh: 琨聞之大悅，率數百騎馳如平城撫納之。
units.en: Liu Kun was overjoyed at the news and raced to Pingcheng with a few hundred horsemen to welcome and settle them.
units.literal: Kun heard and was greatly pleased; he led several hundred horsemen at full gallop to Pingcheng to receive and comfort them.

units.zh: 會石勒攻琨樂平，太守韓據請救於琨。
units.en: Just then Shi Le struck Liu Kun at Le'ping; the prefect Han Ju begged Liu Kun for relief.
units.literal: It happened that Shi Le attacked Kun's Le'ping; the prefect Han Ju requested rescue from Kun.

units.zh: 琨以得雄、澹之眾，欲因其銳，以滅石勒。
units.en: Liu Kun, now reinforced by Xiong and Dan's troops, meant to hurl that fresh strength against Shi Le and destroy him.
units.literal: Kun, having gained the hosts of Xiong and Dan, wished to use their sharp edge to destroy Shi Le.

units.zh: 雄、澹諫曰：「亂民飢疲，未可便用，宜休息觀釁而動。」
units.en: Xiong and Dan urged caution: "These men are hungry, exhausted rebels—not yet fit to throw into battle. Rest them, watch for an opening, then strike."
units.literal: Xiong and Dan remonstrated, saying: "The disorderly masses are hungry and weary and cannot yet be used; it is fit to rest, watch for openings, and then move."

units.zh: 琨不從，使雄、澹率眾討勒，琨屯廣牧為之聲援。
units.en: Liu Kun refused. He sent Xiong and Dan against Le while he held Guangmu to back them.
units.literal: Kun would not follow; he sent Xiong and Dan to lead the host against Le; Kun encamped at Guangmu to sound support.

units.zh: 勒率輕騎與雄、澹戰，澹大敗，率騎千餘，奔于代郡。
units.en: Shi Le met them with light cavalry; Dan was routed and fled north with a thousand riders into Dai.
units.literal: Le led light cavalry to battle Xiong and Dan; Dan was utterly defeated and fled with more than a thousand horsemen to Dai commandery.

units.en: Le sent Kong Chang in pursuit to finish him off.
units.literal: Le sent Kong Chang in pursuit to destroy him.

units.en: Mo Han came from Fanzhi in Yanmen.
units.literal: Mo Han was a man of Fanzhi in Yanmen.

units.en: His family had traded for generations and piled up wealth beyond counting.
units.literal: His family for generations traded goods and amassed wealth in the tens of millions.

units.en: When Liu Kun governed Bingzhou he took Han on as an aide.
units.literal: When Liu Kun held Bing province he summoned Han as an aide.

units.zh: 含居近塞下，常往來國中。
units.en: Han lived near the border and often traveled into the Tuoba realm.
units.literal: Han dwelt near the frontier and often came and went within the state.

units.en: Emperor Mu admired his ability and treated him generously.
units.literal: Emperor Mu loved his talent and capacity and treated him well.

units.zh: 及為代王，備置官屬，求含於琨。
units.en: When he became Prince of Dai he formed a full court and asked Liu Kun to send Han to him.
units.literal: When he became Prince of Dai he fully set up officials and sought Han from Kun.

units.en: Liu Kun sent him, but Han's heart was not in the move.
units.literal: Kun sent him into the state; Han in his heart was unwilling.

units.zh: 琨諭之曰：「當今胡寇滔天，泯滅諸夏，百姓流離，死亡塗地，主上幽執，沉溺醜虜。
units.en: Liu Kun reasoned with him: "Barbarian armies now cover the sky and are snuffing out the Chinese realms; the people wander homeless, the roads are heaped with dead, and our emperor languishes in the hands of savage captors.
units.literal: Kun instructed him, saying: "Today the Hu raiders fill the sky, extinguishing the various Xia; the hundred surnames are displaced, death covers the ground, the sovereign is held in secret imprisonment, drowned among ugly captors.

units.zh: 唯此一州，介在羣胡之間，以吾薄德，能自存立者，賴代王之力。
units.en: Only this province still stands amid the barbarian tide; that I survive at all on my meager merit is because the Prince of Dai upholds me.
units.literal: Only this one province stands among the mass of Hu; that I, with my slight virtue, can preserve myself and stand upright is because I rely on the Prince of Dai's strength.

units.zh: 是以傾身竭寶，長子遠質，覬滅殘賊，報雪大耻。
units.en: I have poured out my person and my wealth, sent my eldest son away as hostage, and staked everything on crushing the remnant enemy and avenging the realm's disgrace.
units.literal: Therefore I pour out body and treasure, send my eldest son far as hostage, and hope to extinguish the remnant bandits and wash away the great shame.

units.zh: 卿為忠節，亦是奮義之時，何得苟惜共事之小誠，以忘出身之大益。
units.en: You are a man of loyalty; this is the hour to act on it. How can you cling to a petty tie of service and forget the far greater good of stepping forward?
units.literal: You, as a man of loyal integrity, are also in a time to rouse righteousness; how can you be sparing of a small bond of service together and forget the great benefit of your own emergence?

units.zh: 入為代王腹心，非但吾願，亦一州所賴。」
units.en: To enter and become the prince's trusted confidant is not only my wish—it is what our whole province depends on."
units.literal: To enter and become the Prince of Dai's trusted center is not only my wish but also what one province relies upon."

units.en: Han at last entered Dai and joined the government.
units.literal: Han then entered Dai and took part in state office.

units.zh: 後琨徙五縣之民於陘南，含家獨留。
units.en: Later Liu Kun relocated five counties' people south of the Xing Mountains; Han's family alone stayed behind.
units.literal: Later Kun moved the people of five counties south of the Xing ridge; Han's household alone remained.

units.zh: 含甚為穆帝所重，常參軍國大謀。
units.en: Emperor Mu held him in the highest regard and kept him at the heart of military and civil strategy.
units.literal: Han was greatly valued by Emperor Mu and constantly took part in great plans of army and state.

units.en: He died holding Left General and Marquis of Guanzhong.
units.literal: He died in office as Left General and Marquis of Guanzhong.

units.zh: 其故宅在桑乾川南，世稱莫含壁，或音訛，謂之莫回城云。
units.en: His old house stood south of the Sanggan River; people still call the place Mo Han's Rampart—or, in a corrupted pronunciation, Mo Hui City.
units.literal: His old residence lay south of the Sanggan River; the world calls it Mo Han's rampart, or through corrupted pronunciation Mo Hui City.

units.en: His son Xian won renown in his own day.
units.literal: His son Xian was famed in the age.

units.en: Under Emperor Zhaocheng he became Left Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the Zhaocheng era he was made Left Palace Attendant.

units.en: Xian's son Ti was likewise a man of counsel.
units.literal: Xian's son Ti also had stratagems.

units.zh: 太祖使題與將軍王建等三軍，討慕容寶廣寧太守劉亢埿，斬之。
units.en: Taizu sent Ti with General Wang Jian and a three-wing army against Murong Bao's Guangning prefect Liu Kangqi and took his head.
units.literal: Taizu sent Ti with the general Wang Jian and the three armies to campaign against Murong Bao's Guangning prefect Liu Kangqi and beheaded him.

units.en: Kangqi's tribes were resettled at Pingcheng.
units.literal: Kangqi's tribes were moved to Pingcheng.

units.zh: 寶上谷太守驎，捐郡逃走，太祖追討，題為大將，別出東道。
units.en: Bao's Shanggu prefect Lin deserted his commandery and fled; Taizu pursued him; Ti was made grand general and took a separate eastern road.
units.literal: Bao's Shanggu prefect Lin abandoned the commandery and fled; Taizu pursued in punishment; Ti was made grand general and marched out by the eastern route.

units.en: For his merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongwan.
units.literal: For merit he was given the enfeoffment Marquis of Dongwan.

units.zh: 及還京師，常與李栗侍宴。
units.en: Back at the capital he often shared the emperor's table with Li Li.
units.literal: When he returned to the capital he constantly attended banquets with Li Li.

units.zh: 栗坐不敬獲罪，題亦被黜為濟陽太守。
units.en: Li was punished for disrespect at court; Ti was demoted as well, to administrator of Jiyang.
units.literal: Li was punished for irreverence in seating; Ti was also demoted to Administrator of Jiyang.

units.zh: 後太祖欲廣宮室，規度平城四方數十里，將模鄴、洛、長安之制，運材數百萬根。
units.en: Later Taizu planned to expand the palace quarter, surveyed dozens of li around Pingcheng, and meant to imitate Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an; millions of timbers were hauled in.
units.literal: Later Taizu wished to enlarge the palaces and measured several tens of li around Pingcheng, intending to model Ye, Luoyang, and Chang'an; timber in the millions of logs was transported.

units.en: Ti's mechanical ingenuity won him summons to oversee the work.
units.literal: Because Ti was ingenious in mechanism he was summoned and ordered to supervise.

units.en: He was called in to debate the right scale and design of the build.
units.literal: He was called in and discussed the fitness of the construction.

units.en: After long attendance Ti grew careless in his duties and was put to death.
units.literal: Ti after long attendance grew somewhat slack; he was granted death.

units.en: Ti's younger brother Yun loved books and excelled at the bow.
units.literal: Ti's younger brother Yun loved learning and was skilled at archery.

units.zh: 太祖時，常典選曹，轉給事中。
units.en: Under Taizu he ran the Selection Bureau and later became palace attendant.
units.literal: In Taizu's time he constantly managed the Selection Bureau and was transferred to Palace Attendant.

units.en: For merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Ande.
units.literal: For merit he was given the enfeoffment Marquis of Ande.

units.zh: 遷執金吾，常參軍國謀議。
units.en: He rose to Commandant of Cavalry and sat in on every major counsel of war and state.
units.literal: He was promoted Commandant of Cavalry and constantly took part in deliberations on army and state.

units.zh: 世祖之克赫連昌，詔雲與常山王素留鎮統萬。
units.en: When Shizu took Helian Chang, he ordered Yun and Prince Su of Changshan to hold Tongwan.
units.literal: When Shizu captured Helian Chang, he issued an edict Yun and the Prince of Changshan Su to remain and garrison Tongwan.

units.zh: 進爵安定公，加平西將軍，後遷鎮西大將軍。
units.en: He was raised to Duke of Anding and General Who Pacifies the West, then to Grand General Who Guards the West.
units.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Anding, with added General Who Pacifies the West; later he was transferred Grand General Who Guards the West.

units.zh: 時初并河西，人心未一，雲撫慰新舊，皆得其所。
units.en: The Hexi had only just been absorbed and loyalties were still divided; Yun soothed old subjects and new until each settled where he belonged.
units.literal: At that time the Hexi region had just been annexed and hearts were not yet one; Yun comforted old and new alike and all found their place.

units.en: He died in the Shenju era and was posthumously titled Duke Reverent.
units.literal: He died in the Shenju era; posthumous title: Duke Reverent.

units.zh: 劉庫仁，本字沒根，劉虎之宗也，一名洛垂。
units.en: Liu Kuren, whose original name was Meigen, belonged to the house of Liu Hu and was also called Lo Chui.
units.literal: Liu Kuren, original style Meigen, was of the lineage of Liu Hu; he had another name, Lo Chui.

units.en: As a young man he was open-handed and bold, with a strategist's mind.
units.literal: In youth he was bold and open, with wisdom and stratagem.

units.en: His mother was born a princess of Emperor Pingwen's house.
units.literal: His mother was a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.

units.zh: 昭成皇帝復以宗女妻之，為南部大人。
units.en: Emperor Zhaocheng married him to another royal clanswoman and made him southern grandee.
units.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng again gave him a clanswoman in marriage and made him southern grandee.

units.zh: 建國三十九年，昭成暴崩，太祖未立，苻堅以庫仁為陵江將軍、關內侯，令與衞辰分國部眾而統之。
units.en: In Jianguo year 39 Emperor Zhaocheng died suddenly before Taizu could be enthroned; Fu Jian made Liu Kuren General Who Commands the River and Marquis Within the Passes and set him with Wei Chen to divide and govern the tribal following.
units.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Jianguo Emperor Zhaocheng died suddenly; Taizu was not yet established; Fu Jian made Kuren General Who Commands the River and Marquis Within the Passes and ordered him with Wei Chen to divide the state's tribes and rule them.

units.zh: 自河以西屬衞辰，自河以東屬庫仁。
units.en: West of the river fell to Wei Chen; east of the river to Liu Kuren.
units.literal: From the river west belonged to Wei Chen; from the river east belonged to Kuren.

units.zh: 於是獻明皇后攜太祖及衞秦二王自賀蘭部來居焉。
units.en: Then Empress Dowager Xianming brought Taizu and the Wei and Qin princes from the Helan tribe to live under Kuren's protection.
units.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager Xianming brought Taizu and the two princes of Wei and Qin from the Helan tribe to dwell there.

units.zh: 庫仁盡忠奉事，不以興廢易節，撫納離散，恩信甚彰。
units.en: Liu Kuren served him with unwavering loyalty, never shifting with fortune's turns; he gathered the scattered and won them with grace, and his trustworthiness was plain to all.
units.literal: Kuren served with full loyalty and did not change his constancy with rise or fall; he gathered and settled the scattered, and his favor and trust were greatly manifest.

units.zh: 苻堅進庫仁廣武將軍，給幢麾鼓蓋，儀比諸侯。
units.en: Fu Jian promoted him to General of Guangwu and granted the insignia of banner, canopy, drums, and parasol, with ceremony equal to a feudal lord.
units.literal: Fu Jian advanced Kuren to General of Guangwu, gave him banner, canopy, drums, and parasol, and ceremonial parity with feudal lords.

units.en: Wei Chen was ranked beneath Liu Kuren.
units.literal: Wei Chen was placed below Kuren.

units.zh: 衞辰怒，殺堅五原太守而叛，攻庫仁西部。
units.en: Wei Chen flew into rage, murdered Fu Jian's administrator of Wuyuan, rebelled, and struck Liu Kuren's western lands.
units.literal: Wei Chen was enraged, killed Fu Jian's Administrator of Wuyuan, and rebelled, attacking Kuren's western territory.

units.zh: 庫仁又伐衞辰破之，追至陰山西北千餘里，獲其妻子，盡收其眾。
units.en: Liu Kuren counterattacked, broke Wei Chen, and chased him more than a thousand li beyond Yin Mountain, seizing his family and absorbing his entire following.
units.literal: Kuren again campaigned against Wei Chen and defeated him, pursuing to more than a thousand li northwest of Yin Mountain, taking his wife and children and gathering all his followers.

units.zh: 庫仁西征庫狄部，大獲畜產，徙其部落，置之桑乾川。
units.en: He marched west against the Kudi, captured vast herds, relocated the tribe, and planted them along the Sanggan.
units.literal: Kuren campaigned west against the Kudi tribe, took great herds and goods, moved their tribes, and settled them on the Sanggan River.

units.zh: 苻堅賜庫仁妻公孫氏，厚其資送。
units.en: Fu Jian bestowed a Gongsun woman on Liu Kuren as his wife and provided her with a rich dowry.
units.literal: Fu Jian bestowed on Kuren's wife the Gongsun clan and enriched her dowry and gifts.

units.zh: 庫仁又詣堅，加庫仁振威將軍。
units.en: Liu Kuren went again to Fu Jian's court and was raised to General Who Quells Might.
units.literal: Kuren again went to Jian and was further made General Who Quells Might.

units.zh: 後慕容垂圍苻丕于鄴，又遣將平規攻堅幽州刺史王永于薊，庫仁自以受堅爵命，遣妻兄公孫希率騎三千，助永擊規，大破之，阬規降卒五千餘人。
units.en: When Murong Chui besieged Fu Pi at Ye and sent Ping Gui against Fu Jian's Youzhou inspector Wang Yong at Ji, Liu Kuren—still loyal to the titles Fu Jian had given him—sent his brother-in-law Gongsun Xi with three thousand horse to help Yong rout Gui and massacre more than five thousand of Gui's men who had surrendered.
units.literal: Later Murong Chui besieged Fu Pi at Ye and also sent a general, Ping Gui, to attack Fu Jian's Inspector of Youzhou Wang Yong at Ji; Kuren, holding himself bound by the titles Jian had granted, sent his wife's elder brother Gongsun Xi with three thousand horsemen to aid Yong in striking Gui; he utterly defeated him and pit-killed more than five thousand of Gui's surrendered soldiers.

units.zh: 乘勝長驅，進據唐城，與垂子麟相持。
units.en: Riding the victory he drove deep, seized Tangcheng, and locked horns with Chui's son Lin.
units.literal: Seizing victory he drove far, advanced and held Tangcheng, and stood in stalemate with Chui's son Lin.

units.zh: 庫仁聞希破規，復將大舉以救丕。
units.en: When Liu Kuren heard Xi had crushed Gui, he gathered a great army to relieve Fu Pi.
units.literal: Kuren heard Xi had broken Gui and again was about to raise a great host to rescue Pi.

units.zh: 發雁門、上谷、代郡兵，次於繁畤。
units.en: He called up the forces of Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai and camped at Fanzhi.
units.literal: He mobilized the armies of Yanmen, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies and halted at Fanzhi.

units.zh: 先是，慕容文等當徙長安，遁依庫仁部，常思東歸，其計無由。
units.en: Earlier Murong Wen and others, slated for resettlement in Chang'an, had taken refuge with Liu Kuren's tribe and longed to go east again but saw no way.
units.literal: Earlier, Murong Wen and others had been due for relocation to Chang'an; they had fled into hiding with Kuren's tribe and constantly thought of returning east, but had no means.

units.zh: 至是役也，知人不樂，文等乃夜率三郡人，攻庫仁。
units.en: On this campaign they saw how little love the levy inspired; Wen and his party struck by night, leading men of three commanderies against Liu Kuren.
units.literal: At this levy they knew men were discontent; Wen and the rest therefore by night led the people of three commanderies to attack Kuren.

units.zh: 庫仁匿於馬廐，文執殺之。
units.en: Liu Kuren hid in the stable; Wen seized him and killed him.
units.literal: Kuren hid in the horse stable; Wen seized and killed him.

units.en: They mounted his best horse and fled to Murong Chui.
units.literal: They took his swift horse and fled to Murong Chui.

units.zh: 公孫希聞亂，自唐城走於丁零。
units.en: Gongsun Xi, hearing of the revolt, abandoned Tangcheng and fled to the Dingling.
units.literal: Gongsun Xi heard of the turmoil and fled from Tangcheng to the Dingling.

units.en: Liu Kuren's younger brother Juan stepped in to govern the tribes.
units.literal: Kuren's younger brother Juan succeeded to take charge of state affairs.

units.zh: 白部大人絜佛叛，[3]眷力不能討。
units.en: Jiefu, grandee of the White Division, rebelled, [3] and Juan lacked the force to crush him.
units.literal: The White Division grandee Jiefu rebelled, [3] and Juan's strength could not subdue him.

units.zh: 乃引苻堅并州刺史張蚝擊佛，破之。
units.en: He called in Fu Jian's Bingzhou inspector Zhang Hao, who defeated Jiefu.
units.literal: He therefore drew in Fu Jian's Inspector of Bingzhou Zhang Hao to strike Jiefu and break him.

units.zh: 眷又破賀蘭部于善無，又擊蠕蠕別帥肺渥于意親山，破之，獲牛羊數十萬頭。
units.en: Juan next routed the Helan at Shanwu and struck the Rouran sub-chief Feiwo at Yiqin Mountain, taking hundreds of thousands of cattle and sheep.
units.literal: Juan again broke the Helan tribe at Shanwu and also attacked the Rouran sub-chieftain Feiwo at Yiqin Mountain, defeated him, and took several hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.

units.zh: 眷第二子羅辰，性機警，有智謀，謂眷曰：「比來行兵，所向無敵，心腹之疾，願早圖之。」
units.en: Juan's second son Luo Chen was quick-witted and full of counsel; he told Juan, "Our armies have known no defeat—but the sickness is within. We should deal with it now."
units.literal: Juan's second son Luo Chen was by nature alert and possessed wisdom and stratagem; he said to Juan: "In recent campaigns wherever we marched we were without match; the trouble in our vitals—I wish we would plan for it early."

units.en: Juan asked, "Who?"
units.literal: Juan said: "Who is it?"

units.zh: 曰：「從兄顯，忍人也，為亂非旦則夕耳。」
units.en: He answered, "Cousin Xian is ruthless. His revolt is only a matter of time."
units.literal: He said: "Cousin Xian is a man who can endure; his rebellion will come not in the morning then in the evening."

units.en: Juan paid no heed.
units.literal: Juan did not take it to heart.

units.zh: 其後，徙牧于牛川，庫仁子顯，果殺眷而代立。
units.en: Later, when the herds were moved to Niuchuan, Liu Kuren's son Xian murdered Juan and usurped his place.
units.literal: Afterward, when the herds were moved to pasture at Niuchuan, Kuren's son Xian indeed killed Juan and replaced him.

units.zh: 羅辰奔太祖，事在外戚傳。
units.en: Luo Chen fled to Taizu; the fuller account stands in the biography of the empresses' kin.
units.literal: Luo Chen fled to Taizu; the account is in the biography of the maternal kin.

units.zh: 顯，本名醜伐，既殺眷代立，又欲謀逆，語在太祖紀。
units.en: Xian, whose birth name was Choufa, after killing Juan and seizing rule plotted treason as well; that story is told in Taizu's annals.
units.literal: Xian, original name Choufa, after killing Juan and replacing him also plotted rebellion; the words are in Taizu's annals.

units.zh: 太祖即位，顯自善無南走馬邑。
units.en: When Taizu was enthroned, Xian fled south from Shanwu toward Mayi.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Xian fled south from Shanwu to Mayi.

units.en: Nuzhen, a kinsman of the line, brought his following in to submit.
units.literal: A clansman, Nuzhen, led his division in submission.

units.en: His elder brother Jian had long lived among the Helan.
units.literal: Nuzhen's elder brother Jian had earlier dwelt with the Helan tribe.

units.zh: 至是，奴真請召犍而讓部焉。
units.en: Now Nuzhen asked to call Jian in and turn the tribe over to him.
units.literal: At this time Nuzhen asked to summon Jian and yield the division to him.

units.en: Taizu, approving the act, allowed it.
units.literal: Taizu, moved by the righteousness of it, granted his request.

units.zh: 犍既領部，自以久託賀訥，德之，乃使弟去斤遺之金馬。
units.en: When Jian took command, he felt himself long beholden to He Ne and sent his brother Qujin with a gift of a golden horse.
units.literal: Once Jian held the division, deeming himself long indebted to He Ne for shelter, he sent his younger brother Qujin to present him with a golden horse.

units.zh: 訥弟染干因謂之曰：「我待汝兄弟厚，汝今領部，宜來從我。」
units.en: He Ne's brother Ran'gan told him, "I have been generous to you two; now that you lead a division, you should come over to my side."
units.literal: He Ne's younger brother Ran'gan then said to him: "I have treated you brothers generously; now that you lead a division, you ought to come follow me."

units.en: Qujin put the matter to Nuzhen.
units.literal: Qujin asked Nuzhen about it.

units.zh: 奴真曰：「父為國家附臣，世効忠貞。
units.en: Nuzhen replied, "Our father was the state's man; our house has served with loyalty for generations.
units.literal: Nuzhen said: "Our father was a subject attached to the state; for generations we have served with loyal fidelity.

units.en: I meant to keep our name whole, and that is why I yielded the tribe.
units.literal: I sought to preserve our name and honor intact, and for that reason I yielded the division.

units.zh: 今汝等無狀，乃欲叛主懷貳。」
units.en: Now you act shamefully and would turn traitor with a double heart."
units.literal: Now you behave disgracefully and would betray your lord with divided hearts."

units.en: He killed Jian and Qujin on the spot.
units.literal: He then killed Jian and Qujin.

units.zh: 染干聞其殺兄，率騎討之，奴真懼，徙部來奔太祖。
units.en: Ran'gan, hearing his brother had been killed, led cavalry against him; Nuzhen in alarm moved his people to seek refuge with Taizu.
units.literal: When Ran'gan heard that he had killed his elder brother, he led horsemen to attack him; Nuzhen in fear moved his division to flee to Taizu.

units.zh: 太祖自迎之，遣使責止染干。
units.en: Taizu rode out to meet him and sent envoys to rebuke Ran'gan and make him stop.
units.literal: Taizu went out in person to welcome him and sent envoys to reprimand Ran'gan and halt him.

units.zh: 奴真感恩，請奉妹充後宮，太祖納之。
units.en: Nuzhen, moved by the grace shown him, offered his younger sister to the inner palace, and Taizu took her.
units.literal: Grateful, Nuzhen offered his younger sister for the inner palace; Taizu took her.

units.zh: 後太祖討顯于馬邑，追至彌澤，大破之。
units.en: Later Taizu attacked Liu Xian at Mayi, chased him to Mize, and broke him completely.
units.literal: Later Taizu campaigned against Xian at Mayi, pursued him to Mize, and routed him utterly.

units.zh: 衞辰與慕容垂通好，送馬三千匹於垂，垂遣慕容良迎之。
units.en: Wei Chen was on good terms with Murong Chui and sent him three thousand horses; Chui sent Murong Liang to meet the herd.
units.literal: Wei Chen maintained friendly relations with Murong Chui and sent him three thousand horses; Chui dispatched Murong Liang to receive them.

units.en: Liu Xian smashed Liang's force and drove off the horses.
units.literal: Xian defeated Liang's army and seized the horses.

units.zh: 垂怒，遣子麟、兄子楷討之，顯奔馬邑西山。
units.en: Chui in fury sent his son Lin and his brother's son Kai to punish him; Xian fled into the western hills of Mayi.
units.literal: Chui in anger sent his son Lin and his brother's son Kai against him; Xian fled to the western hills of Mayi.

units.zh: 麟輕騎追之，遂奔慕容永於長子。
units.en: Lin pressed him with light horse until he took refuge with Murong Yong at Changzi.
units.literal: Lin with light cavalry pursued him, and he fled at last to Murong Yong at Changzi.

units.zh: 部眾悉降於麟，麟徙之中山。
units.en: His whole following submitted to Lin, and Lin moved them to Zhongshan.
units.literal: All his followers surrendered to Lin, and Lin resettled them at Zhongshan.

units.en: Liu Xian's brother Kang'ai is treated in the Empresses' biography.
units.literal: Xian's younger brother Kang'ai: the account is in the Empresses' biography.

units.zh: 史臣曰：始祖及桓、穆之世也，王迹初基，風德未展。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Under the Founding Ancestor and Emperors Huan and Mu, the royal work had barely begun and moral influence had not yet spread.
units.literal: The historiographer says: In the age of the Founding Ancestor and of the Huan and Mu emperors, the royal enterprise had only just been laid, and exemplary virtue was not yet fully displayed.

units.zh: 操、含託身馳驟之秋，自立功名之地，[4]可謂志識之士矣。
units.en: Cao and Han threw themselves into the hurrying age of war and carved out a place of merit and renown, [4] — true men of purpose and sight.
units.literal: Cao and Han betook themselves to the season of galloping campaigns and made their own ground of merit and fame, [4] — men who may be called of purposeful mind and vision.

units.zh: 劉庫仁兄弟，忠以為心，盛衰不二，純節所存，其意蓋遠，而並貽非命，惜乎！
units.en: The Liu Kuren brothers took loyalty for their heart and did not shift between rise and fall; the pure constancy they kept looked far ahead — yet both died before their time. What a loss!
units.literal: The brothers Liu Kuren held loyalty as their heart; in fortune or decline they did not waver; the pure integrity they preserved showed purpose reaching far — yet both met untimely ends. A pity!

units.en: Textual notes
units.literal: Collation notes

units.zh: 操立碑於大邗城南 錢氏考異卷三八云：「此傳載衞操所立碑……惜為史臣改竄，失其本真。
units.en: Wei Cao set up a stele south of Dahang city. In Qian's Textual Notes, juan 38, we read: "This biography records the stele Wei Cao erected; alas, the historiographers altered it and its original authenticity was lost.
units.literal: Cao erected a stele south of Dahang city. Qian's Textual Notes, juan 38, state: "This biography records the stele Wei Cao erected; alas, the court historiographers altered it and its original truth was lost.

units.en: The opening line runs, 'Scion of the Yellow Emperor of Wei.'
units.literal: At the head of the inscription it reads: 'Scion of the Yellow Emperor of Wei.'

units.zh: 考其時未有魏號，以文義度之當云『鮮卑拓跋氏』也。
units.en: At that date there was no Wei designation yet; by sense it should read 'of the Xianbei Tuoba clan.'
units.literal: On examination, at that time there was as yet no title of Wei; judged by the sense of the text it ought to read 'of the Xianbei Tuoba clan.'

units.zh: 碑為猗㐌而立，必書晉所授官爵及猗㐌、猗盧二人名，篇乃稱『桓穆二帝』，亦史臣所改。」
units.en: The stone was raised for Yiyi and must have named the Jin-bestowed offices and both Yiyi and Yilu; calling them 'the two emperors Huan and Mu' is another historiographer's change."
units.literal: The stele was erected for Yiyi; it must have recorded the offices and ranks granted by Jin and the names of Yiyi and Yilu, yet the text calls them 'the two emperors Huan and Mu' — again an alteration by the historiographers."

units.zh: 外動亦攘 北史卷二０本傳「動」作「勳」。
units.en: "Outward campaigns also repelled": Northern History juan 20, this life, has xun (merit) where this text has dong (campaign).
units.literal: "In outward campaigns, he also repelled": in Northern History juan 20, this biography reads dong (campaign) as xun (merit).

units.zh: 按「外勳亦攘」，意為對外有攘患之功，碑末有「勳攘大患」句也是此意。
units.en: Note: "outward merit also repelled" means merit in repelling foreign trouble; the stele's closing "merit that repelled the great scourge" is the same idea.
units.literal: Commentary: "In outward merit he also repelled" means he had the achievement of repelling external calamity; the inscription's closing line "merit that repelled the great scourge" bears the same sense.

units.en: It seems "xun" (merit) is right.
units.literal: It seems "xun" (merit) is correct.

units.zh: 白部大人絜佛叛 諸本「白」作「曰」。
units.en: "The Bai tribe's great chief Jiefo rebelled": editions read bai (Bai) as yue (say).
units.literal: "The great chief Jiefo of the Bai tribe rebelled": in various editions bai (white/Bai) is written as yue (say).

units.en: Cefu, juan 352
units.literal: Cefu juan 352

units.en: 〈folio 4180〉
units.literal: 〈page 4180〉

units.literal: reads "bai" (White/Bai).

units.zh: 按卷一序紀力微之三十九年稱：「夏四月祭天，諸部君長悉來助祭，唯白部大人觀望不至。」
units.en: Note: Annalistic Preface, juan 1, Liwei year 39: "Fourth month, summer sacrifice to Heaven; every division's chief came to assist — only the Bai tribe's great chief held back and did not attend."
units.literal: Commentary: Juan 1, Annalistic Preface, year 39 of Liwei states: "In the fourth month of summer they sacrificed to Heaven; the chieftains of all divisions came to assist in the rites — only the great chief of the Bai tribe stood apart and did not come."

units.zh: 又猗盧之三年稱「白部大人叛入西河」。
units.en: Yilu year 3 also says "the Bai tribe's great chief rebelled and entered Xihe."
units.literal: Again, year 3 of Yilu states "the great chief of the Bai tribe rebelled and entered Xihe."

units.en: "Yue" is a corruption; emended per Cefu.
units.literal: The character "yue" is erroneous; the text is now emended according to Cefu.

units.zh: 自立功名之地 諸本無「名」字。
units.en: "Carved out a place of merit and renown": editions omit ming (fame).
units.literal: "Made their own ground of merit and fame": various editions lack the character ming (fame/name).

units.zh: 殿本考證云：「『功』字下北史
units.en: Palace Edition textual notes: "After the character 'gong' (merit), Northern History
units.literal: Palace Edition textual notes state: "Below the character 'gong' (merit), Northern History

units.en: 〈juan 20〉
units.literal: 〈juan 20〉

units.en: has 'ming'; that text should stand."
units.literal: has the character 'ming'; that reading should be accepted."

units.zh: 按「功名」與上「馳驟」對文，這裏脫「名」字，今據北史補。
units.en: Note: "merit and fame" pairs with "hurrying" above; the word ming dropped here and is restored from the Northern History.
units.literal: Commentary: "merit and fame" balances with "galloping" above; here the character ming has dropped out; supplied now according to Northern History.
